provenance.variable_identity: Bound indices are de Bruijn offsets in the exact term; free/schematic names retain their Isabelle type and index.
provenance.limitations: Typed elaborated terms, not surface syntax. Uses are occurrences, not alias/liveness analysis. Unknowns stay explicit.

boundaries.basis: HOL.bool has exactly the two constructors constant:HOL.True and constant:HOL.False.
conditions: Map to Rust bool with exactly true and false.
Do not introduce a three-valued or truthy representation.
Boolean results are consumed only by source conditionals.

boundaries.basis: HOL.True is a nullary constructor of HOL.bool.
conditions: Map to Rust true.
It has no runtime computation or arguments.
It must be usable as a HOL.If condition.

boundaries.basis: HOL.False is a nullary constructor of HOL.bool.
conditions: Map to Rust false.
It has no runtime computation or arguments.
It must select the else branch in HOL.If equations.

boundaries.basis: HOL.If execution equations are `if False then x else y = y` and `if True then x else y = x`.
conditions: Use a Rust if-expression in the owning function; no recursive translation of HOL.If internals.
Evaluate the condition exactly once.
Evaluate only the selected branch.
The then and else expressions must have the same Rust type.
Preserve the source branch order in insort.

boundaries.basis: Orderings.preorder extends Orderings.ord and contributes a source ordering constraint, not an executable source equation in this program.
conditions: Represent as a marker/supertrait obligation folded into the shared Linorder trait rather than an empty emitted trait.
Preserve generic polymorphism through `T: Linorder`.
Do not add runtime assertion checks for preorder axioms.

boundaries.basis: Orderings.ord declares the source parameters constant:Orderings.ord_class.less_eq and constant:Orderings.ord_class.less of type `'a => 'a => bool`.
conditions: Expose `less_eq(&self, &Self) -> bool` and `less(&self, &Self) -> bool` on the shared Linorder trait.
`less_eq` is the only source method used by the business equations.
Do not assume numeric operands or a concrete instance.
Equality must be consistent with the supplied order instance.

boundaries.basis: Orderings.order extends Orderings.ord and Orderings.preorder; it supplies ordering axioms but no executable equations used here.
conditions: Fold the marker constraint into Linorder; no separate empty Rust trait is required.
Preserve source polymorphism at the `T: Linorder` boundary.
Do not add unsupported runtime order checks.

boundaries.basis: Orderings.linorder extends Orderings.ord, Orderings.order and Orderings.preorder; the source functions are polymorphic over this class.
conditions: Define `pub trait Linorder: PartialEq { fn less_eq(&self, other: &Self) -> bool; fn less(&self, other: &Self) -> bool; }` in the shared order-support component.
Provide a blanket implementation for `T: Ord` mapping `less_eq` to `<=` and `less` to `<`; custom instances may also implement the trait.
The instance must be a linear order; do not substitute a sorting algorithm or an unrelated comparison.
Do not silently fall back to a different comparison when no instance exists.

boundaries.basis: Orderings.ord_class.less_eq is a class parameter of Orderings.ord and is used by insort in the source condition `x \<le> y`.
conditions: Call the trait method as `x.less_eq(&y)` with borrowed operands.
True includes equality; equal elements take the then-branch.
Do not rewrite as strict less-than or as `!(y < x)` unless the concrete instance justifies it.
No arithmetic, wrapping, truncation or overflow behavior is involved.

boundaries.basis: List.list is a recursive datatype with constructors List.list.Nil and List.list.Cons; all source list equations are structural.
conditions: Use `Vec<T>` (or `type List<T> = Vec<T>`) in the list-support component.
Preserve element order and multiplicity exactly.
Empty vector corresponds exactly to Nil; nonempty vector decomposes as head plus tail.
Do not impose a sorted invariant except where insort/isort establish it.
Do not use sets, deduplication, or unordered worklists.
Map to `Vec::new()` or an empty `List<T>`.
It has zero elements.
It is not an aliased shared sentinel requiring mutation semantics.

boundaries.basis: List.list.Cons has fields `'a` and `List.list 'a`; source equations use `x # xs`, `x # y # ys`, and `y # insort x ys`.
conditions: Construct a sequence with the head at the front and the tail order unchanged.
Duplicates are retained; no membership-based insertion.
With an owned Vec tail, use owned prefixing/insertion at the front; do not clone solely to preserve source aliasing that the source does not observe.
`x # []` is the singleton sequence.
